study: Short-circuit failed public tests before compilation
scope: Two cached upload draft artifacts, one failed and one passed. Alternate original/short-circuit verification order. Every original public test and exact-lock Worker compile remains unchanged. Failed public tests can skip compilation but never pass. Paired model-free verification timing only; no inference/workflow/generalization speed claim.

method.candidateSelection: One recorded failed upload draft and one recorded passing upload draft, selected after their outcomes were known. These are verification fixtures, not unseen evaluation tasks.
method.comparison: Same original public tests, exact test counts, artifacts, cached dependency image, protected execution and Worker compiler. Original first on failure; short-circuit first on success. One run per method and artifact, each in its own sandbox.
method.acceptance: Only valid passing public tests with exact expected count and zero skips can invoke compilation. Rejection marks compilation skipped and passed=false. Accepted candidates must pass compilation. Full acceptance grading is unchanged.
method.measurement: Elapsed time surrounds each complete verifier, including sandbox cleanup. Serial local wall-clock samples; no confidence interval or inference/workflow latency claim.
method.reproducibility: Raw private fixtures and reports are hash-pinned. Public report omits source artifacts, prompts and raw diagnostics.

decision.reason: Both methods agree on public outcomes and final acceptance. Failed public tests avoid a redundant compiler call; passing candidates still compile. The failing sample saved about 0.54 seconds. This is a local verifier optimization, not proof of faster end-to-end fusion.
